name: Klickitat River
blurb: Fast, milky, glacier-fed river in a basalt canyon above the Columbia Gorge.

sections.notes: Remote canyon through WDFW's Soda Springs Wildlife Area. Watch for wood. Both ends are WDFW water-access sites: Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass required.

putInAccess.operator: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
putInAccess.sourceName: WDFW Facilities GIS, Boat Ramp layer (feature 166, 'Leidl', concrete)
putInAccess.note: Coordinate is WDFW's own boat-ramp feature, separate from its site and parking points. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25) puts it on the campground-side bank edge, a few metres from open water. Legal access: the WDFW Leidl page (https://wdfw.wa.gov/places-to-go/water-access-sites/leidl-1640) lists it in the Soda Springs Wildlife Area Unit, open year-round, with 1 concrete ramp and camping. The WaterAccessSites layer shows it managed by WDFW with no closure. A Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass is required.
putInAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
putInAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~307 on the flowline), the ramp is about 27 m right of the NHD centreline. Matches imagery, v1 and AW.

takeOutAccess.operator: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
takeOutAccess.sourceName: WDFW Facilities GIS, Boat Ramp layer (feature 317, 'Mineral Springs', concrete)
takeOutAccess.note: Coordinate is WDFW's own boat-ramp feature. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25) puts it at the water's edge beside a cleared launch patch, not in the campground. Legal access: the WDFW Mineral Springs page (https://wdfw.wa.gov/places-to-go/water-access-sites/mineral-springs-1655) lists it in the Mineral Springs Wildlife Area Unit, open year-round, with 1 concrete ramp. WaterAccessSites shows it WDFW-managed with no closure. Pass required. This is the 'Icehouse' access: take-out for Leidl-Icehouse and put-in for Icehouse-Turkey Hole.
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~225), the ramp is about 22 m right of the NHD centreline, on the west/north-west bank. Confirmed on imagery.

sections.notes: Ishi Pishi (Class III) is just above Turkey Hole — scout. About 2 hr at a relaxed pace (AW reports). Both ends are WDFW water-access sites: Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass required. Turkey Hole is take-out only (WDFW).

takeOutAccess.operator: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
takeOutAccess.sourceName: WDFW Facilities GIS, Hand Launch layer (feature 914, 'Take-out', comment 'Take-out only.', edited 2025-02)
takeOutAccess.note: Coordinate is WDFW's own hand-launch/take-out feature, separate from the parking-area point (45.73986, -121.22888). Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25) puts it on the south bank under tree cover, about 10 m from open water. Legal access: the WDFW Turkey Hole page (https://wdfw.wa.gov/places-to-go/water-access-sites/turkey-hole-1534) says 'Turkey Hole (RM 4.8) is the last WDFW-designated take-out above Lyle Falls... This launch is for take-out only' and warns of hazardous water and active tribal fishing downstream. WDFW-managed, no closure. Pass required. Do not continue downstream.
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~255), the take-out is about 23 m left of the NHD centreline, on the south bank. The WDFW parking point is also south. Confirmed on imagery.

mapAuditNote: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 1). All three endpoints (Leidl, Mineral Springs/Icehouse, Turkey Hole) are verified. Coordinates come from WDFW's Facilities GIS ramp/hand-launch features, checked on Esri World Imagery. Access comes from WDFW water-access pages and the WaterAccessSites layer (WDFW-managed, no closure). Banks come from NHDPlus HR flowlines. Turkey Hole is take-out only and the last designated take-out above Lyle Falls.
